title: sylabis registry index (paths.json)
description: Static, serverless index of published sylabis paths. Served raw (GitHub Pages, sparse-index style); clients cache it with a daily TTL and ETag revalidation. Human-readable companion doc: docs/registry/schema.md in the sylabis repo.

id.description: Author-scoped listing id: <author-slug>/<path-slug>. The author segment must match the listing author's GitHub handle (namespace-squatting policy: first PR from the matching handle wins the namespace).

git_url.description: Public repo hosting the published template bundle. Repo naming convention: sylabis-path-<slug> (Homebrew-tap style).

commit_sha.description: PINNED commit. Clients attach exactly this commit; a repo whose history no longer contains it is refused (sha mismatch).

topic.description: Free-text topic line, matched by `sy paths search`.

license.description: SPDX id from the bundle's publish manifest (default CC-BY-4.0). Mandatory — bundles ship source LOCATORS, never harvested source text, so the license covers the course structure and lesson text.

assumed_knowledge.description: Declared assumed-knowledge tags (replaces the scrubbed learner block).

author.description: Author handle, credited on listings and attribution chains.

verified.description: Badge fields set by registry CI ONLY — never by the listing PR author. A green verify-listing run writes them; the re-verification cron refreshes them.

sylabis_version.description: sylabis version that ran the verification checks.

checks_passed.description: Which gates ran green, e.g. self_test, okf_conformance, okf_hashes, pii_scan, secret_scan, source_locators.

derived_from.description: Optional attribution chain: the source (listing id or git URL) this path was derived from. Surfaced on listings — attribution fuels the status-based reciprocity mechanic.
